publish.title: What is an index fund? A two-minute explanation
publish.description: What an index is, how a fund tracks it, and why it is not risk-free. Education, not advice.

scenes.headline: What is an index fund?
scenes.narration: You have probably heard that index funds are a simple way to invest. Here is what that means.

scenes.headline: First, an index
scenes.narration: An index is a list of companies used to measure a market. The S and P 500, for example, tracks five hundred large United States companies.

definition.meaning: A list of companies that measures a market. The S&P 500 tracks 500 large US companies.

scenes.headline: How a fund tracks it
scenes.narration: An index fund simply buys the companies in an index. When you invest, you own a small slice of all of them.

scenes.headline: Index fund or one stock
scenes.narration: Spreading money across many companies reduces the damage if one of them fails. Putting it all in one company does not.

left.label: Index fund
left.text: Spread across many companies, usually low fees

right.label: Single stock
right.text: All your money rides on one company

scenes.headline: Not risk-free
scenes.narration: An index fund can still fall when the market falls. Diversification reduces the risk of one company failing, not the risk of the whole market.

scenes.headline: Compare the fees
scenes.narration: Fees are the part you can control, so compare them. This is education, not advice.
